newsitem.title: EGYPT: Moslem militants kill five in southern Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Moslem militants kill five in southern Egypt.

text.p: Suspected Moslem militants on Friday killed five people and wounded a woman in separate attacks on two villages in Egypt's south, security sources said.

They said the gunmen, believed to be members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) fighting the government, shot dead police captain Fasah Abdel Kareem Ali and assistant Abdel Tawab Younis who were part of a convoy guarding Safay village, some 240 km (150 miles) south of Cairo.
In the nearby Nantout village, other Gama'a gunmen killed butchers Salah Abdel Hakeem and Abu Zeid Moez while they were walking down the street.
The militants thought the men were police informers, the sources said. Farmer Mohamed Ibrahim Ahmed, 65, was killed and farmer Hoda Fadl also wounded in the attack.
The Gama'a, Egypt's largest Moslem militant organisation, has been fighting for four years to overthrow the government of Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
The group has targeted Christians, tourists, policemen and government officials during its armed campaign. Last April, it claimed responsibility for killing 18 Greek tourists in Cairo.
More than 960 people have been killed and scores wounded in the political violence.
